title: Right fraction calculus for globally finite filtered complexes
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\mathcal H_f(R)$ have as objects integer cochain complexes of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration], each with some integers $a<b$ such that $F^aK=K$ and $F^bK=0$ as complexes. The bounds may depend on the object. Its morphisms are filtration-preserving chain maps modulo homotopies $h^n:K^n\to L^{n-1}$ with $f-g=dh+hd$ and $h^n(F^iK^n)\subseteq F^iL^{n-1}$. Define $\operatorname{gr}^iK=F^iK/F^{i+1}K$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients], and let $W$ be the morphisms inducing quasi-isomorphisms on every $\operatorname{gr}^i$.
Then $W$ contains identities, is closed under composition, satisfies two-out-of-three, and admits a calculus of right fractions. Explicitly:
(1) for $f:X\to Z$ and $s:Y\to Z$ with $s\in W$, there are $t:T\to X$ in $W$ and $g:T\to Y$ such that $f\circ t=s\circ g$ in $\mathcal H_f(R)$;
(2) for $f,g:X\to Y$ and $s:Y\to Z$ in $W$ with $s\circ f=s\circ g$, there is $t:T\to X$ in $W$ such that $f\circ t=g\circ t$.
The objects $T$ in these assertions also have a globally finite filtration; no cochain-degree bound is required.

proof.text: Apply the fully proved graded two-out-of-three theorem and identity theorem. These give the multiplicative property required by the fraction structure.

For an arbitrary left fraction, use the right Ore square on its numerator and denominator, then package the witnessing object, quasi-isomorphism and map as a RightFraction. Its square equation is exactly the required fraction equation.

Apply the separate right cancellation theorem to the two maps and the postcomposed denominator. Package its witnessing quasi-isomorphism and equality as the ext field. Pair the resulting right-fraction structure with the proved two-out-of-three property.
